findings.text: A newcomer learns what Athena is in the first sentence, and the next two paragraphs explain that this page is a study and what a study is. The opening works.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository."

findings.text: The page says why it exists: it is a demonstration. Anyone can check that by following any [cN] link to a pinned file and line, so the evidence for 'why it matters' sits on the page itself.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim, and every claim to lines in the project's own files."

findings.text: The page names these selling points but never shows them. Nothing here shows a checker model or a cost figure, so a newcomer has to take the main features of Athena on trust.
findings.source: Header lede: "has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost."

findings.text: The next step is easy to find; the header links to it. But it gives no prerequisites (Rust toolchain, model API keys), no clone command, and doesn't say which repository `athena ask` will change. A newcomer would need the GitHub README before acting.
findings.source: Next steps: "Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh" and "Try it with a one-line request: athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: Almost all of the page is detailed firstmate internals: exit codes, pending-close records, places-held. Yolo, green and in scope are each defined two to four times. A newcomer who came for Athena may give up before reaching Next steps, which is why the header link to it matters.

The studied project is also explained plainly before any jargon, and the 'Words used first' list defines terms before they are used. That makes the dense sections readable for someone willing to go on.
findings.source: Start here: "Firstmate is a tool that keeps a backlog of programming tasks and hands each one to a separate AI coding tool, called a worker"

findings.text: The page is honest that nothing was run. That builds trust, but it also tells a newcomer the demo shows reading only, not Athena changing code, which is the main job the lede describes.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f1: "no failure or retry edge was observed; every claim is marked read."

findings.text: This sentence is confusing on first reading. The definitions actually come right after it, before the cards.
findings.source: Transitions lead-in: "The two deciders are explained below the cards' heading."
